note: EVAL-1's gate (ADR-0028 decision 5). The three quality axes are absolutes and stay that way: this suite is small enough that any scenario failing is a regression, not noise. The two cost axes are ceilings, and they are calibrated differently on purpose. tokens_mean is environment-independent — a deterministic corpus through a deterministic composition — so it sits at roughly twice what this suite measures, tight enough that a composition which starts spending double is caught. latency_p95_ms is not environment-independent at all: a debug-profile gateway on a shared CI runner is nothing like a laptop, so this ceiling is a shape detector for an order-of-magnitude change (measured ~16ms here) and emphatically not an SLO. knowledge_update is MEM-5's category axis (ADR-0039 decision 14) and is an absolute for the same reason the other quality axes are: with dedup off — the state `a_pack_can_turn_the_feature_off` puts the product in, and the state it was in before MEM-5 — an ADD-only store composes the superseded fact beside its replacement, both scenarios' `must_not_contain` fails, and the axis reads 0.0. Any value below 1.0 is therefore the feature regressing rather than noise. EVAL-3 owns the real LongMemEval corpus and its judge; this axis measures the same category on this suite's fixtures. EVAL-6 owns latency under load, EVAL-4 owns retrieval quality with real embeddings, EVAL-2 owns extraction precision, EVAL-5 owns the zero-tolerance policy-leak gate. Nothing here is a target for any of them. `--update-baseline` rewrites floors to what a run achieved and ceilings to half again above what it cost.
